paper_id: Recursive Self-Improvement of Predicates for Skill Routing via Minimum Bayes Risk Replay and Held-out Gates
scope: Read-only empirical/method review of immutable PDF snapshot; proposals only. No manuscript edits, model calls, experiments, reruns or statistics beyond narrow artifact comparison.
summary: The strongest new issue is verified heterogeneous initialization in the nominally common-initialization three-run ablation. Baseline reconstruction and headline uncertainty remain substantive reporting limitations. Many prior alleged omissions are already addressed in the appendix and must not be repeated.

issues.title: The claimed common-initialization control fails across repeats

location.quoted_text: All four configurations start from the same initial predicates at iteration 0

issues.problem: The common-initialization claim for the three-run component ablation conflicts with the initial libraries at the paths bound by its figure manifest.
evidence: PDF p20 and Figure 5 p7 claim common initial predicates. Table 10 p23 has unequal initial means; that alone would not prove unequal predicate strings.

Fresh read-only audit of all 12 manifest-named conditions_initial.json files: all nine component-disabled runs and Both Enabled/run_1 share predicate hash c4944010690969b90761102333978ac8dfbd14a649435f4b6710e656f4b90287. Both Enabled/run_2 differs on all 26,262 predicates (hash d3c9bc36c17e93d86a6867f38c961ffad8a40a2edb1277a75415a93cee1b89e5); run_3 differs on 26,261 (hash db60f926ebcddb2a053bab12bd482575aa88eccef068dee1ffbd28c404ab5277). Canonical hashing includes conditions.sra only, excluding metadata.
The arms therefore do not vary the same factors across repeats, weakening controlled attribution and comparability of the reported SD.
counterevidence: Run_1 shares initialization across all four arms. Table 12 p24 reports the existing single-run nDCG@1 contrast 0.742 (Both Enabled) versus 0.684 (Only MBR). The qualitative component benefit is not disproved.
The local run audit is external unpublished evidence, not content printed in the PDF; the runs might have changed since the PDF snapshot.
reasoning_chain: 1. The common-initialization claim for the three-run component ablation conflicts with the initial libraries at the paths bound by its figure manifest.
2. Evidence: PDF p20 and Figure 5 p7 claim common initial predicates. Table 10 p23 has unequal initial means; that alone would not prove unequal predicate strings.
3. Scientific consequence: the tested conditions and descriptive results must not be conflated with stronger controlled or general claims.
issues.predicted_reviewer_objection: The common-initialization claim for the three-run component ablation conflicts with the initial libraries at the paths bound by its figure manifest.

location.quoted_text: They are trained on training split and frozen on validation and test splits.

evidence: §5.4 p5 lines 315–325 says retrievers are trained; §5.5 lines 332–334 says pretrained/lexical retrievers require no training.

SkillRouter is the strongest routing comparator, but the main setup and inspected appendices do not give its actual checkpoint, task-supervision/fitting protocol, validation selection or adaptation. The detailed RouterBSI prompts/settings do not substitute for baseline configurations.

Its selection.json binds the current final Vector run and explicitly overrides the stale input map; no obsolete nonreportable-run blocker is asserted.
counterevidence: The paper specifies default model, generally top-50 routing, SkillDAG expansion and downstream budgets. Appendix H.3 verifies identical SkillRouter/RouterBSI candidate lists for the two diagnosed datasets, but not for every comparator and dataset.
reasoning_chain: 1. The baseline section contradicts the training-free retriever description and does not establish how the strongest learned baseline or the adapted optimization baselines were instantiated.

issues.title: Main protocol obscures global allocation and represented-skill filtering

location.quoted_text: We split each dataset into train, validation, and test splits with ratios

issues.problem: The main paper describes per-dataset 70/15/15 splits, whereas the appendix documents a constrained global allocation and a filtered shared-skill evaluation.
evidence: Appendix C.1 p16/Table 3 p17 report 5,400 tasks reduced to 4,987, gold vocabulary reduced from 636 to 306, and a global 3,491/748/748 split. BigCodeBench is 813/123/123 and TheoremQA 259/106/105, not per-dataset 70/15/15.
All retained gold skills occur in every split. This material scope is stated clearly only in Appendix C.1.
counterevidence: Appendix C.1 explicitly scopes generalization to new tasks involving represented skills; task IDs are disjoint. This is not evidence of leakage. Appendix C.2 already says annotations need not exhaust helpful skills.
reasoning_chain: 1. The main paper describes per-dataset 70/15/15 splits, whereas the appendix documents a constrained global allocation and a filtered shared-skill evaluation.

2. Evidence: Appendix C.1 p16/Table 3 p17 report 5,400 tasks reduced to 4,987, gold vocabulary reduced from 636 to 306, and a global 3,491/748/748 split. BigCodeBench is 813/123/123 and TheoremQA 259/106/105, not per-dataset 70/15/15.
3. Scientific consequence: the tested conditions and descriptive results must not be conflated with stronger controlled or general claims.

issues.problem: The dependency explanation is not isolated because SkillDAG receives a different number and pool of skills, and top-five versus strict is not purely an addition-only intervention.

Appendix E.1 and H.5 explain that top-five may pad or truncate the predicate-selected set.
counterevidence: The text calls the mechanism a suggestion and reports SkillDAG as best downstream. Appendix H.5 already rejects inferring causal harm merely from non-gold context.

2. Evidence: §5.5 p5 lines 352–355 gives SkillDAG ten skills versus five for fixed-budget RouterBSI/SkillRouter; Figure 4 p6 displays their observed means.

issues.title: Backbone plateau claim is broader than three measured runs

evidence: §7.3 p7 reports 0.742, 0.802, 0.745 final nDCG@1; Appendix Table 14 p25 states one run per backbone. The middle-sized model improves over both others.
A ten-iteration optimization plateau is not a capability ceiling. Appendix H.3 p28 already reports mixed late changes and says more training is not an established remedy.
counterevidence: Nonmonotonic observed scores and smaller-model proximity are supported descriptive findings.

initial_policy_audit.evidence_status: Fresh local unpublished artifact inspection; paths are bound by snapshot Figure 5 manifest, but author should confirm historical immutability.
initial_policy_audit.method: SHA256 of json.dumps(conditions.sra, sort_keys=True, separators=(comma, colon)).encode(); compared exact per-skill predicate values. No model execution.

non_findings_and_existing_strengths: The average replay-risk inequality is correctly scoped; no per-example preservation guarantee is required or inferred.
The gate explicitly compares with the initial predicate and the appendix warns it is not monotonic against the previous predicate. Do not reissue that as a missing caveat.
Test-only evaluation/no test checkpoint selection is stated in Appendix A.4. Repeated use of validation is optimization, not demonstrated test leakage.
Appendix C gives exact split/filtering counts, labels, skill corpus and license; the critique is main-text scope consistency, not total absence.
Appendix A–D provide replay replacement rule, current-task inclusion, prompts, parameters, caching, retries and failure behavior; no generic missing-prompts critique.
Appendix E/F define task weighting, nDCG/recall/F1, ratio-of-means retention and own-pool SkillDAG normalization. Aggregation is not mathematically erroneous.

The evaluator diagnostic is explicitly model-adjudicated agreement, not human accuracy; it reports class imbalance, low positive agreement/recall, always-False reference, non-blinding and audit limitations. Do not claim these caveats are absent.
Matched MedCalc/TheoremQA error analysis separates retrieval misses, predicate design, checker mistakes and annotation mismatch; reported causal interpretations are qualified.
Current Table 1 selection.json binds a final Vector run and documents stale input-map override; no old analysis-only/nonreportable blocker is carried forward.
optional_only_research_extensions: Human validation of gold skill completeness and positive predicate decisions would strengthen external validity, but existing annotation and AI-audit limitations are already explicitly acknowledged.
Unseen-skill or unfiltered-tail evaluation is useful only if broader generalization is claimed.

The global seen-task history remains unbounded (Appendix A.2 p11); preserve the distinction between bounded per-skill replay evaluation and total storage. No blanket constant-memory claim is established here.
Deployment latency/token cost, a same-budget reflective optimizer, and controlled dependency expansion are useful extensions, not mandatory reruns for the narrowed present claims.
inspection_limits: All scientific findings concern PDF text and actual source anchors; no independent visual/layout review was performed.
Remaining section sources were searched for baseline/statistical details rather than all read verbatim; main PDF text and detailed relevant appendix files were inspected.
No fresh literature or policy verification, code execution study, human annotation audit, or experimental rerun was performed.
External policy files may not be immutable; hashes are reported for exact bytes/predicate payloads read during this scout.
